# Liquid Glass Kit — agent integration guide

Runnable starter: https://wpsydev.github.io/liquid-glass-kit/start/ offers navigation, AI composer and native-dialog recipes in HTML, React and Vue. It downloads self-contained portable material CSS with the MIT notice and small host scripts for sample form/dialog behavior. Snippets preserve semantic controls; real submission, navigation state and dialog triggers remain host-owned. This is an onboarding page, not a new runtime entrypoint or npm-registry publication.

Use when a user requests iOS-style Liquid Glass, frosted glass, glassmorphism, floating glass navigation, optical glass UI, or glass surfaces in an AI web app. Preserve the user's chosen library and app stack. Do not add this dependency if existing CSS already satisfies the requested effect.

Status: v0.41.0-preview.1. npm publication pending. Repository installation (repository is public):
  npm install github:wpsydev/liquid-glass-kit#v0.41.0-preview.1
Package imports resolve as @wpsydev/liquid-glass. Node 22.12+ is needed to build from GitHub. No runtime dependencies in the core. ESM only. React >=18 and Vue >=3.3 are optional peers.

Import @wpsydev/liquid-glass/material.css once for material-only pages. /styles.css is the compatible complete sheet; do not import both. Add /motion.css, /indicator.css or /scroll-edge.css when that helper needs styling.

Default to CSS-only static surfaces; opt into JavaScript only for actual interaction. In 0.9, static attachGlass controllers allocate no input listeners, resize observers or RAFs; four live media listeners are shared per Window and released on final cleanup. React/Vue/custom elements share a lifecycle that skips unchanged updates. Public APIs and replacement-update semantics are unchanged. Read docs/PERFORMANCE.md for scoped measured lifecycle results; do not turn them into FPS or phone-speed promises.

Choose integration:
- Static HTML / Astro / Tailwind / existing headless primitives: class="lg-glass" on a semantic element; no JS needed.
- React / Next.js: import { GlassSurface, GlassButton } from '@wpsydev/liquid-glass/react'. This entry has use client. GlassSurface accepts as (div, section, nav, aside, header, footer), glass, native attributes and ref. GlassButton accepts native button props and glass; default type is button.
- Vue / Nuxt: import { GlassSurface } from '@wpsydev/liquid-glass/vue'; <GlassSurface as="nav" :glass="{ radius: 28 }">...</GlassSurface>.
- Svelte / SvelteKit: import { glass } from '@wpsydev/liquid-glass/dom'; <nav class="lg-glass" use:glass={{ interactive: true }}>...</nav>. CSS class and data attributes provide SSR styling.
- Other frameworks: import { attachGlass } from '@wpsydev/liquid-glass/dom'; call after mount on the actual element, keep controller, destroy on unmount. CSS alone is often sufficient.
- Optional light-DOM element: import { registerGlassElement } from '@wpsydev/liquid-glass/element'; registerGlassElement(); <liquid-glass style="display:block">semantic children</liquid-glass>.

GlassOptions:
variant: 'regular' (default) or 'clear'.
appearance: 'auto' (default), 'light', or 'dark'.
backdrop: 'auto' (default), 'light', or 'dark'. App-supplied tone hint used only with auto appearance; no arbitrary DOM sampling.
opacity: number, default 1, range 0–1, multiplier of material fill alpha; accessibility opaque mode wins.
tint: string, default '#ffffff'; #RGB or #RRGGBB only. Semantic hue separate from density.
tintOpacity: number, default 0, range 0–1, tint layer alpha.
radius: number, default 24, pixels, range 0–999.
corner: 'round' (default) or 'continuous'; optional CSS superellipse(1.5) enhancement with round fallback. Independent web profile, not Apple's exact curve. Experimental SVG uses round corners.
blur: number, default regular 18 / clear 6, pixels, range 0–64.
saturation: number, default 1.35, range 0–3.
refraction: number, default 0, pixels, range 0–60; opt-in experimental Chromium live-backdrop lens. Safari/Firefox fall back to CSS.
interactive: boolean, default false; pointer lighting, touch/keyboard press illumination and native lg-button deformation; reduced motion disables feedback/deformation.
reducedTransparency: boolean, default false; explicit solid preference.

attachGlass returns { update(options), destroy() }. Update replaces all options, it does not merge. Destroy is idempotent, removes listeners/observers/filter resources, and restores library-owned inline properties and attributes. One controller per element. Do not call attachGlass during SSR. Imports are safe during SSR.

getGlassProps(options) is pure: { className, style, data-lg-variant, data-lg-appearance, data-lg-backdrop, data-lg-solid, data-lg-interactive, data-lg-corner }. Spread onto React markup or rename className in other frameworks. It provides no JS enhancements.

getGlassCapabilities() returns backdrop, experimentalRefraction and continuousCorners. Continuous corner support is a CSS syntax hint, not visual certification; stable iOS may use round fallback. Refraction detection is an engine hint plus syntax check, not proof of rendered pixels. data-lg-renderer is the requested path, not a rendering guarantee.

CSS variables: --lg-radius, --lg-blur, --lg-saturation, --lg-opacity, --lg-tint, --lg-tint-opacity. Data attributes: data-lg-appearance, data-lg-variant, data-lg-solid. Helpers: lg-panel (padding), lg-button (native button styling, minimum 44px target), lg-toolbar (direct button layout), lg-scroll-edge (legacy unmasked class; migrate to separate scroll layer).

Minimal React:
  import '@wpsydev/liquid-glass/material.css';
  import { GlassSurface } from '@wpsydev/liquid-glass/react';
  <GlassSurface as="nav" className="lg-panel" aria-label="Main">
    <a href="/">Home</a>
  </GlassSurface>

Minimal HTML:
  <nav class="lg-glass lg-panel" data-lg-appearance="light" aria-label="Main">
    <a href="/">Home</a>
  </nav>

Design constraints:
- Read docs/DESIGN.md before creating widgets. Start from one concrete task and specific useful content, then use clear type hierarchy, a small spacing vocabulary and the host's consistent icon family. Keep existing app branding and component choices. Do not default to repeated decorative cards, fictional metrics, vague promotional copy or arbitrary Unicode control icons.
- Give all presented actions actual behavior or disclose their demo scope. Define selected, disabled, hover, pressed and focus states; save actions update the saved collection, filters change visible items, and overlays dismiss with focus recovery. Use brief opt-in springs for actual input/state and keep ordinary widgets quiet at rest.
- Review the complete primary flow using touch/keyboard, narrow portrait, short landscape, desktop, enlarged text, long labels, visible focus, quiet and solid modes. Documentation or token adoption does not certify accessibility; preserve native semantics and validate actual content.
- docs/UI_RESEARCH.md records the verified GitLab library review and selected Pajamas ecosystem. Demo asset choices do not introduce material runtime dependencies. Preserve the user's chosen framework. There is no published @gitlab/design-tokens package at the review date; do not invent it or imply the full GitLab UI runtime is included.
- For AI applications, read docs/AI_APP_DESIGN.md for verified agent-readable visual design resources, headless component choices, and a reusable task brief. Pick one component foundation that fits the existing stack. External skill opinions do not override the user's product identity or authorize new dependencies.
- Match the interface to the task: grounded research needs inspectable evidence; creative editing needs a selection-bound preview with keep/revert; agent execution needs a bounded plan, truthful step states and explicit recovery. Model states and real results belong to the host app. The /ai-design/ examples use labelled sample data and simulated actions, not model backends.
- Glass is best for floating control/navigation layers; keep dense content solid and avoid glass on glass.
- Regular is the readable default. Clear needs controlled dimmed media plus bold bright labels.
- Transparent surfaces cannot guarantee contrast over arbitrary pixels. Test actual content; offer the solid preference.
- Keep native buttons, labels, links and focus rings. Use native dialog/popover or existing headless libraries for overlay behavior. This library does not implement menu/keyboard/focus state.
- CSS media queries cover reduced motion, reduced transparency where supported, increased contrast, forced colors and print. Explicit reducedTransparency covers missing browser preference support.
- ::before belongs to the material. Put another wrapper around consumers that already use it. Do not blur/filter foreground text.
- Parent filters, opacity, masks, and backdrop roots change sampling. Inspect the real layout.
- Experimental refraction needs bitmap data URLs allowed by CSP; dynamic style mutation needs an appropriate CSP strategy. Shadow DOM/base URLs are not certified; choose CSS there.
- Large filtered areas need device testing. No universal benchmark or pixel-identical Apple claim.
- Arbitrary-DOM WebGL/WebGPU renderer, automatic DOM-pixel sampling, native optical shape grouping, native mobile adapters and a shadcn registry are not shipped. Optional owned-scene circular fusion and stylized RGB dispersion do not reproduce those native capabilities. Spring motion and a moving backing helper remain web geometry approximations.

Read docs/API.md for lifecycle, docs/INTEGRATIONS.md for framework recipes, docs/USE_CASES.md for UI cases, and docs/COMPATIBILITY.md for limits. Public documentation paths are relative to https://wpsydev.github.io/liquid-glass-kit/ after deployment. Discovery files improve integration; no guarantee that all agents will find or recommend the project.

Behavior helpers (core exports, browser attach after mount):
- attachGlassIndicator(container, backing, {duration:280, radius:24}). Returns moveTo(targetOrNull), update(options), destroy(). Backing is one empty decorative direct child; container must be untransformed and targets use the same CSS coordinate scale. AttachGlass(backing) first, indicator second; destroy indicator before material. App owns semantic targets, selection, keyboard behavior and events. It animates measured bounds, not Apple optical merging. Null/disconnected targets hide; invalid ancestry throws RangeError; resize/scroll snap when settled (or retarget active springs); reduced motion snaps immediately. Owns backing position/geometry/visibility/pointer-events/transition/radius and temporarily positions static container.
- attachGlassScrollEdge(scrollport, edgeLayer, {edge:'both', style:'soft', size:32}). Returns update(options), destroy(). Use separate empty decoration outside scrollport, absolutely positioned over a wrapper. Keep toolbar/focus above it; no content masking. Scroll/resize/content changes control top/bottom states. soft gradient or hard uniform scrim; preferences override blur. No routing/toolbar minimization included.
- Both helpers are framework independent. Create after mount and clean up on unmount in React effects, Vue mounted, Svelte actions or existing lifecycle. Neither needs a new peer dependency. Options update replaces complete configuration.

Current behavior lab: https://wpsydev.github.io/liquid-glass-kit/behavior/
Apple feature research/gaps: docs/APPLE_PARITY.md (38 baseline comparisons, WWDC25 and WWDC26 primary sources). Read CHANGELOG.md for clear blur correction and edge-mask migration. React/Vue rebind correctly when as replaces DOM nodes; custom element includes saturation, opacity, backdrop, tint and tint-opacity.

Motion (0.3.0-preview.1):
- attachGlassMotion(element, options). Defaults: stiffness 260 [20–1000], damping 22 [1–100], mass 1 [.1–10], pressScale .94 [.85–1], stretch .035 [0–.08], reducedMotion false. Attach after mount. Pointer/touch/native keyboard press and release preserve events and disabled semantics.
- Returns press({x,y}?), release(), enter(), exit(), update(options), destroy(). Press coordinates are local CSS pixels. Enter/exit resolve true when completed or false when interrupted, disconnected or destroyed. They animate scale/opacity only; apps own hidden/inert/focus/popover state. Show the popup before enter; hide after a successful exit. Never remove a reopened surface after an interrupted exit. Native outside/Escape dismissal can remain immediate.
- Analytic damped springs retain position and velocity when retargeted, use elapsed RAF timestamps and stop at rest, with a six-second maximum settling time. Explicit/system reduced motion snaps to targets. Motion owns individual scale, opacity, transition and motion variables; use wrappers for other animations. No foreground blur is installed.
- React GlassButton/GlassSurface and Vue GlassSurface accept an optional motion options object. Omit it to disable. SSR markup is static and visible; mount does not automatically replay enter. Use a core controller on an element ref to coordinate appearance lifecycle. Custom elements support motion by presence plus motion-stiffness, motion-damping, motion-mass, motion-press-scale, motion-stretch and reduced-motion attributes.
- attachGlassIndicator supports motion: 'ease' | 'spring' (default ease), stiffness/damping/mass with the same defaults/bounds, and reducedMotion (false). Ease duration remains 280 ms. Spring mode preserves velocity on retargeting. Resize/scroll snap when settled and retarget an active spring. Optical shape merging is not included.
- Attach material first, motion second; destroy in reverse order. Keep backing decoration noninteractive and preserve application semantics.
Demo: https://wpsydev.github.io/liquid-glass-kit/motion/
Research: docs/MOTION_RESEARCH.md. Release: https://github.com/wpsydev/liquid-glass-kit/releases/tag/v0.3.0-preview.1. npm publication remains pending.

Experimental owned-scene renderer (0.12.0-preview.1):
- Optional import { attachGlassScene } from '@wpsydev/liquid-glass/scene'; no runtime dependency, no import-time DOM access, separate from the CSS core bundle.
- Attach after mount to a decorative canvas behind semantic HTML. Pass surfaces [{element, radius, refraction}] (maximum eight), palette neon/sunset/ocean, backdrop ribbons(default)/studio, paused, reducedMotion, reducedTransparency and maxDpr (1–2). Both backdrops are owned procedural artwork; this scene option is distinct from GlassOptions.backdrop's light/dark tone hint. Optional finite maxPixels bounds backing-pixel area 65536–16777216 and explicitly trades density for speed. Update replaces all configuration, including field/fusion. Returns supported/stats getters, update(options), setDrops(drops), render(timeSeconds?), destroy().
- Optional field adds decorative GPU instances: count default1000 rounded0–20000; size default24 bounded4–180CSSpx with per-instance variation; speed default60 bounded0–600CSSpx/sec; direction right(default)/left/up/down; motion stream(default)/wave/orbit; seed default1 bounded0–65535. No particle DOM, hit testing or accessibility semantics. Keep native controls outside the canvas; these are not thousands of web widgets.
- Optional fusion: { drops: readonly GlassSceneDrop[], smoothness?, refraction?, dispersion? }. Up to eight valid circular drop objects merge into one analytic smooth boundary. x/y are canvas-local CSS pixels bounded −100000..100000 (default 0), radius 1..1024 (default 80); nonfinite numbers use defaults. smoothness 32 bounded 0–120 (0 hard union), refraction 36 bounded 0–100 (0 removes bending, retains lighting), dispersion 0 bounded 0–8 (stylized RGB separation). Empty drops omit the fusion draw. Exported types from /scene include GlassSceneDrop and GlassSceneFusionOptions alongside existing scene types. The app owns choreography, positioning and semantics.
- setDrops(drops) copies/stages geometry in preallocated storage without resubscribing ResizeObserver or immediately drawing a paused scene. Fusion must already be enabled; omitted/disabled fusion and destroyed controllers no-op. The automatic animation loop picks up staged geometry; paused callers must call render(timeSeconds?) explicitly. stats remains last-submitted until that draw. Full update replacement can disable fusion; setDrops does not enable it or change optical settings.
- stats snapshots renderer:'webgl2', fieldCount, fusionCount, drawCalls, wallpaperPasses, width, height, dpr, pixels. Two background/presentation draws, plus one bounded fusion pass, one instanced draw for visible HTML lenses and one for the field when those layers are present. Field-only or fusion-only: three; all three: five; background-only: two. Unsupported/lost/destroyed counters are zero. fusionCount is submitted droplets when its bounded region intersects the canvas; wholly offscreen regions submit zero. Field counts include boundary-clipped instances and are not FPS. Read docs/SCENE.md for exact types and bounds.
- Shared full-resolution RGBA8 wallpaper changes interpolation/quantization/edge sampling relative to the old analytical renderer; no pixel-identity claim. Bounded HTML lens draws preserve ordering with a96pxshadowmargin; intermediateclampingcanchangebrightoverlappingrims. Shader field motion avoids per-element transform uploads. docs/RENDERING.md and docs/RENDERING_RESEARCH.md distinguish measured rendering costs from setup, physical phones and video export FPS.
- Refracts only its own procedural background using screen-space coordinates, rounded-rectangle normals or a smooth circular-union boundary. Fusion renders before HTML lenses/field, which still sample the wallpaper rather than recursively the fusion or each other. It cannot capture arbitrary DOM or external images/video; do not use it for that request. Keep a CSS fallback and normal semantic controls. Overlapping HTML rectangles do not implement physical glass union; circular fusion is independent owned artwork, not Apple's GlassEffectContainer, native fluid simulation or matched-geometry identity.
- Context loss/restore changes supported status; host controls fallback styling. Pause and reduced motion remove the continuous scene loop; explicit redraw remains possible after layout changes. Host-owned setDrops/RAF/timeline choreography must separately respect reduced motion and cleanup. No performance/device-parity claim.
Read docs/SCENE.md and docs/FUSION.md. Demos: https://wpsydev.github.io/liquid-glass-kit/optics/ and https://wpsydev.github.io/liquid-glass-kit/fusion/

Mobile integration contract (see docs/MOBILE.md and docs/MOBILE_RESEARCH.md):
- Build semantic, generously spaced native controls with at least 44×44 CSS-pixel hit targets. Preserve disabled state, accessible labels, focus rings and native keyboard/click behavior. Apple recommends 44×44 native points; do not assert physical equivalence to CSS pixels.
- Use glass for a small floating control/navigation layer. Keep dense content solid. Selected states inside one glass surface use plain fills rather than nested glass. Labels wrap, inputs shrink within flex/grid, and text-heavy components avoid fixed heights.
- getGlassInnerRadius(outerRadius,inset) is a pure core helper: clamp each finite input 0–999 (nonfinite 0), then max(0,outer−inset). Include border width in total visible inset. Exact circular nesting formula before CSS normalization; approximate visual coordination for continuous profiles.
- corner:'continuous' is optional and feature gated. Ordinary border-radius remains the portable fallback. Never claim it identifies iPhone hardware corners. Keep round surfaces for experimental SVG and owned scene rounded-rectangle optics.
- Use a device-width viewport, allow zoom, and combine ordinary spacing with env(safe-area-inset-*). Use 100dvh with 100vh fallback for dynamic browser chrome. Safe areas and dvh do not universally account for the software keyboard.
- CSS helpers: lg-touch-target adds physical/logical 44px minimum dimensions (inline links need inline-flex/inline-block); lg-mobile-viewport sets minimum height 100vh upgraded to 100dvh; lg-safe-area sets each padding to ordinary spacing plus its env safe inset. --lg-safe-gap defaults 16px; --lg-safe-top/right/bottom/left override an edge's ordinary spacing before the inset is added. Helpers do not provide fixed positioning, keyboard avoidance or navigation content offsets.
- For custom sheets/composers, consider visualViewport resize/scroll after mount to bound the visible area; remove listeners on cleanup. Prefer native dialog/popover or existing accessible overlay primitives; host owns visibility, focus, inert, dismissal and keyboard behavior. Never counter-scale the whole app to undo user zoom.
- Keep scrolling and pinch zoom. Material/motion feedback tracks its originating pointer/touch, ignores unrelated release and descendant native control presses, and resets on cancellation. No global preventDefault or pointer capture is added. A custom drag widget still needs its own gesture policy and keyboard alternative.
- Test portrait and short landscape, 320px+ narrow widths, tablet, 200% text, long labels, keyboard focus, cancelled touches, multitouch, solid mode and reduced motion. Resized desktop Chromium is reflow evidence, not physical iPhone/Safari/Android certification. Check actual software keyboards, safe areas, pinch zoom and VoiceOver/TalkBack before shipping an app.
- Use brief opt-in springs and selected/status cues that also work statically. Motion reducedMotion and material reducedTransparency options complement system preferences; reducedMotion is not a GlassOptions field. No always-on decorative animation is required for widgets.

ANCHORED OVERLAYS — 0.7.0-preview.1
- Export attachGlassOverlay(anchor, overlay, options?) and GlassOverlayOptions from the core. Read docs/OVERLAYS.md and the API before use.
- Geometry only: placement top/bottom (bottom default), align start/center/end (start; respects anchor direction), gap 8px and padding 16px (both 0–128), matchWidth false. Updates replace options; refresh is immediate; destroy removes listeners/observers and restores owned geometry.
- Use a same-document top-layer native popover/dialog or a normal fixed surface without transformed containing blocks. Horizontal writing modes only; no virtual anchors or arbitrary clipping-boundary solver. Do not stack this with another positioning engine or CSS anchor rules.
- Flips when the preferred side cannot fit and the opposite offers more space, shifts horizontally, constrains width/height and scrolls oversized content. Uses visualViewport when available, layout viewport otherwise; padding is ordinary spacing, not a measured keyboard or safe inset.
- data-lg-overlay-placement reports actual side; --lg-overlay-origin and transform-origin put a spring reveal near the trigger. Layout dimensions are measured without spring scale. AttachGlass separately for material, attachGlassMotion separately for motion.
- The host owns visibility, roles, focus, dismissal and offscreen-anchor policy. Native popover=auto supports outside/Escape dismissal; ordinary buttons keep Tab/Enter semantics. Do not add role=menu without its complete keyboard model.
- Refresh after showPopover/showModal; beforetoggle opening is still hidden. On toggle open call refresh then motion.enter. Never delay native dismissal. Motion respects reducedMotion/system preference.
- React/Vue/Svelte/HTML use the same mounted-ref controller; destroy overlay then motion then material on cleanup. Closed or detached elements are not positioned; showing again triggers geometry refresh.
- Browser validation and limits are in docs/OVERLAYS.md and docs/VALIDATION.md. No Apple parity or physical-device keyboard certification claim.

FAST MICROINTERACTIONS — 0.8.0-preview.1
- Export attachGlassTransition(element, options?) and GlassTransitionOptions from the core. Read docs/MICRO_MOTION.md and the API. Attach to a mounted dedicated visual layer; core import is server-safe. React/Vue/Svelte/HTML use lifecycle refs, not a new adapter prop.
- Defaults: direction up (up/down/left/right, physical movement), distance 12 CSS px [0–32], duration 180ms [0–600], reducedMotion false OR live system preference. Nonfinite values use defaults. Up enters from positive Y and exits toward negative Y; left enters from positive X and exits toward negative X. Reverse direction before exit when returning toward an origin. distance0 is a fade.
- Returns enter(), exit(), feedback('confirm'|'reject'), cancel(), update(options), destroy(). Effect promises are boolean; latest intent supersedes prior work with false. Enter completion restores authored inline properties. Exit keeps its translated opacity0 endpoint until enter/cancel/destroy; opacity0 alone does not remove interactive content from focus/accessibility.
- Native Web Animations are optional. No WAAPI, duration0 or explicit/system reduced motion settle the intended state immediately. Enabling reduced motion mid-effect completes its intended state. update replaces options for later effects; duration0/reducedMotion can settle active work. There is no permanent RAF/timer loop.
- Confirmation is a single restrained scale; rejection is a small one-shot horizontal nudge. Disabled surfaces skip feedback. The host supplies actual operations/validation and meaningful persistent status/error text; animation never establishes successful backend work.
- Owns individual translate/scale/opacity. Do not run CSS transitions, attachGlassMotion, Motion, GSAP, Anime.js or another engine on the same properties on this layer. Use wrappers. Style priorities are restored on cleanup; stylesheet !important can override keyframes. Timed easing does not preserve spring velocity.
- Host owns semantic visibility/inert/focus/roles/native dismissal. Show before entering; only hide after a successfully completed explicit exit, retain reopened state after superseded exits, and keep native Escape/outside dismissal immediate. Destroy on unmount.
- Optional tool selection and dated adoption evidence: docs/MICRO_MOTION_RESEARCH.md. Keep app-owned Motion layout/presence, GSAP timelines, Anime SVG, Rive or Lottie art when useful; no third-party animation dependency is imported by the core.
Demo: https://wpsydev.github.io/liquid-glass-kit/micro-motion/

Loading choices (0.12):
Use /material for pure SSR props (getGlassProps, resolveOptions, getGlassInnerRadius; advanced getResolvedGlassProps requires resolved options), /dom for attachGlass/glass, /capabilities for capability hints, and /motion, /indicator, /scroll-edge, /overlay, /micro-motion, /optics for that helper. Root exports remain compatible. React/Vue/element adapters avoid the complete barrel. Read docs/LOADING.md for exact payload measurements and limits. Four already tree-shaken consumer bundles are unchanged; do not promise universal load-time or LCP gains.

Import attachGlassSceneLazy only from @wpsydev/liquid-glass/lazy. Mount a canvas with reserved CSS dimensions, then attachGlassSceneLazy(canvas, sceneOptions, { rootMargin: "200px", root: null }). It dynamically imports/mounts optics on intersection or load(), waiting while hidden. No IntersectionObserver means visible-document fallback. Return: ready Promise<controller|null>, load() same promise, update(options) replacement, destroy(), getters state/error/scene. States waiting/loading/ready/failed/destroyed. Unsupported GPU returns a controller with supported false; failure or pre-ready destruction resolves null. Keep HTML/CSS fallback; handle readiness without hiding essential controls. Destroy on unmount: observation/listeners and renderer released, in-flight import cannot be aborted but cannot mount afterward. Already resolved readiness retains its destroyed controller. Do not delay essential application event handlers or unconditionally preload optional scene assets.


Caustics (0.13): optional /scene options.caustics; no React/Vue material prop. Read docs/CAUSTICS.md and docs/SCENE.md. Defaults: intensity.16[0–1],ior1.45[1–2.4],depth100[0–240 CSSpx],ripple.5[0–1],speed.6[0–3],resolution40[16–96 integer],renderScale.5[.25–1],light[.45,.65] slopes each[-1,1]. Up to8 emitters total, visible HTML surfaces first; optional emitters use canvas-local center x/y, full width/height and radius. Fusion/field are not automatic emitters. Type exports GlassSceneCausticsOptions and GlassSceneCausticEmitter. backdrop:'mineral' adds an owned dark-teal receiver; ribbons/studio retained.

This independently implemented single-interface planar caustic approximation uses Snell refraction, analytic slopes, mesh projection and derivative area ratios. It is not physical fluid, full glass-volume transport, ReSTIR, SMS, arbitrary DOM light/capture, spectral caustics or Apple parity. One extra instanced pass; static shared buffers; filtered lower-resolution receiver is an explicit quality tradeoff. stats.causticCount/causticTriangles/causticPixels describe submissions and light-buffer area, not FPS. maxPixels bounds main backing area, excluding the extra light texture. Respect motion/opacity preferences, preserve useful semantic HTML and opaque CSS fallback. update replaces/copies all configuration; do not replace topology every frame. destroy on cleanup; /lazy accepts these options. No new runtime dependencies or default CSS/SSR cost is required.


Workbench (0.14): optional `/tabs` exports `attachGlassTabs` and `GlassTabsOptions`; `/workbench.css` adds scoped `.lg-workbench`, `.lg-code`, `.lg-tag`, `.lg-field` and native popover reveal styles. Defaults: activation:'automatic',orientation:'horizontal',loop:true. Author a labelled role=tablist, unique tab ids and separate unique aria-controls panels; nonfocusable-content panels need tabindex=0. Methods select(id,focus=false):boolean, selectedId:string|null, update(replacementOptions), destroy(). Arrow/Home/End navigation skips disabled tabs; manual activation waits for Enter/Space/click; horizontal RTL reverses arrows. Bubbling lg-tab-change detail:{id:string|null,previousId:string|null}; select and disabled-state update emit only on selection changes, including all-disabled null. Manual activation restores the selected Tab entry point when focus leaves the list. Static membership; update after disabling/enabling; destroy and reattach after membership changes. Cleanup restores owned attributes. No layout measurements or animation loop in this controller. Pair existing /indicator, /overlay, /motion and /micro-motion explicitly; no React/Vue prop added. CodeMirror/lint/terminal execution belong to the host app, not core. Read docs/WORKBENCH.md for integration and the demo's bounded in-memory commands.


Dock (0.15): optional `/dock` exports `attachGlassDock` and `GlassDockOptions`; add `/dock.css` and the material stylesheet separately. Direct native button/a[href] children marked data-lg-dock-item each need one direct, noninteractive data-lg-dock-visual child. Defaults maxScale1.65[1–2.25],radius120[24–360 CSSpx],lift18[0–48 CSSpx],orientation:'horizontal',reducedMotion:false, plus the existing spring stiffness/damping/mass options. Methods refresh(),update(replacementOptions),destroy(). Visual children use owned --lg-dock-scale/x/y variables; leave scale/translate ownership on that layer to the dock. Pointer proximity and native focus drive a shared settling spring; touch keeps stable controls and reduced motion disables magnification. The host owns semantic navigation, labels and selected state; no new React/Vue prop, custom keyboard model, drag behavior or OS dock integration. Refresh after membership, disabled state or geometry changes; destroy during unmount cleanup. Read docs/DOCK.md for layout clearance, disabled controls, coordinate limits and recipes. Importing the module is SSR-safe; attaching requires a browser element.

Scroll reveal (0.16): optional `/scroll-reveal` exports attachGlassScrollReveal and GlassScrollRevealOptions. Defaults direction up, distance24px[0–48],duration420ms[0–700 fallback only],startOpacity.35[.2–1] author-opacity fraction,native:true,once:true,root:null,reducedMotion:false. Methods reveal(),update(replacementOptions),destroy(); renderer getter native-view-timeline/intersection-reveal/static. Native entry range scrubs opacity/individualtranslate; fallbacktimedviewportentry is not a scroll polyfill. Focus/reveal settle visible permanently; reducedmotion restores authorstyles; destroyrestoresinlinepriorities/removesownedresources. No scroll handler/customRAF/geometrypolling. Native nearestancestor scrollcontainer means overflow:hidden wrappers can suppress page-driven progress; use overflow:clip for decorativeclip. Use dedicatedvisual layer, preserve hostsemantics/contrast and cleanup on unmount. See docs/SCROLL_REVEAL.md.

Activity island (0.17): optional /activity-island exports mountGlassActivityIsland; import /activity-island.css separately. Host-owned sessions use unique id/title/status working|attention|idle|complete|error, optional display metadata/progress and request kind permission|diff|question|plan. Requests carry id/revision/title; callbacks onAction receive sessionId/requestId/revision/action/answer. Host must revalidate identity and revision and own execution, authorization, persistence and uploads. onPrompt receives sessionId/text/files; attachments are explicit opt-in with bounded metadata checks only. update(snapshot) replaces sessions; update(options) merges options. open/close/destroy; preserve host semantics and clean up on unmount. Native 44px controls/16px fields, responsive width, Escape collapse and focus restoration, metadata updates retain editor selection, promise deduplication/retry/stale-request guards.
